projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained 22-25 device count with zero camera motion at 10:46 PM on a Monday strongly suggests either overnight guests or heavy stationary entertainment (gaming/streaming) rather than typical nighttime quiet; worth confirming to rule out unauthorized access or unnecessary energy use.

The sustained 23-27 device count alongside zero camera motion at 9:44 PM strongly indicates a network registration artifact or untracked guest network rather than actual occupancy, as the household's combined devices would not sustain this count without triggering camera alerts.

The persistent presence count of 23-26 devices contradicts zero camera activity, indicating likely false positive detection from network noise or unregistered IoT devices that may be triggering incorrect automations.

The presence count consistently shows 24-27 devices while cameras record zero activity during a typical active Monday afternoon, indicating the tracker is likely counting smart home IoT devices or network artifacts rather than actual people, or that the cameras are offline. Steve should verify camera status and presence filtering to ensure accurate monitoring.

The presence count is fluctuating between 22-28 devices while cameras show zero activity, indicating the count is likely driven by background IoT devices or network scanning rather than human movement. This mismatch is worth monitoring to rule out network instability or unexpected guests.

The presence count has stabilized at 22 devices with zero camera activity over the past hour, confirming the earlier drop reflects normal device sleep or expected Monday afternoon departure rather than an unmonitored event. This cross-signal pattern indicates the household is in a settled, expected midday state.

The presence count has shifted down from the previously flagged 28-29 to a stable 23-24 between 11:40 and 12:14, indicating the house remains occupied but with fewer active devices. Combined with zero camera activity, this suggests a quiet, active home rather than an empty one, which may warrant a quick check if family schedules changed or if it's a holiday/weekend.

The network maintains a stable 28-29 device count with rapid oscillations, indicating a dense IoT environment or a specific device cycling its connection rather than human movement. The lack of a device count drop at 09:19 AM suggests the children may still be home or their devices are stationary, warranting a quick check if they've left for school.

The network shows a steady increase in connected devices from 26 to 29 between 03:42 and 07:09, followed by minor fluctuations. This pattern aligns with smart home systems waking up and family members connecting their phones as the morning routine begins, indicating normal pre-school/day activity rather than an anomaly.

The sustained 26–28 device count combined with zero camera motion and both adults logging ~10-hour sleep sessions confirms the household is in a prolonged, undisturbed rest period rather than hosting guests, validating the existing flags as benign.
